name: Oracle
thesis: STUB: Oracle (ORCL) is an evaluation candidate — a mature enterprise-software franchise (database, applications) re-accelerating on the back of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) and a surge in AI-training capacity demand, evidenced by a step-change in remaining performance obligations (RPO). The bull case is OCI compounding while the legacy base provides cash flow; the offset is an aggressive, partly debt-funded data-center capex ramp that has compressed (and at times negated) free cash flow. Needs user-authored thesis + tier_1_kpis (RPO growth, OCI/cloud revenue growth, cloud as % of total, capex, net leverage) + DCF params if/when it graduates to portfolio.
key_driver: OCI/RPO compounding vs. debt-funded data-center capex pressuring FCF
thesis_breakers_qualitative: RPO durability — the AI-training RPO surge is concentrated; watch how much converts to recognized OCI revenue vs. slips or is renegotiated.

FCF under capex ramp — capex for OCI buildout has overwhelmed operating cash flow; a prolonged FCF deficit funded by rising debt is the balance-sheet risk, distinct from the legacy franchise's cash generation.
Cloud-transition optics — total revenue growth can stay modest while OCI compounds; judge the thesis on cloud/OCI growth and RPO, not blended top line.

break_rules.narrative: Revenue declining YoY for 2 consecutive quarters — outright top-line contraction.

GAAP operating margin negative for 2 consecutive quarters — operating loss. (FCF-margin and capex-intensity universals deliberately omitted: Oracle's deliberate OCI capex ramp has compressed/negated FCF, so those floors would false-breach for a company that is investing on purpose — judge FCF via per-ticker calibration instead.)
GAAP net income negative for 2 consecutive quarters — bottom-line loss.

business_model_rules.narrative: Total revenue YoY < 5% for 2Q — STUB; the OCI-led reacceleration thesis requires blended growth to hold up as cloud mix rises. Sub-5% sustained signals the cloud ramp is no longer outrunning legacy decay.
GAAP operating margin < 25% for 2Q — STUB; Oracle's GAAP op margin runs ~30%+. A sustained drop below 25% would signal OCI buildout/operating costs overwhelming the franchise's profitability.
